# What the data-dict export loses: American Time Use Survey (ATUS)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2003-2025` |
|---|---|
| variables exported | 641 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 21 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 195 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 6 |
| quantities exported with open range bounds (no valid range recorded) | 593 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 14,501 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 4,046 |
| groups (batteries, subjects, sections), not exported | 18 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 |
